name: tabhand

tools.name: browser_open_tab
tools.description: Open a new tab in the user's own Chrome, with their logins, and optionally load a URL. The tab opens in the background inside this session's tab group: Chrome is not brought to the front and the user's tabs are untouched, so they can keep working. Returns the tabId the other browser tools need.

url.description: Page to load, e.g. https://example.com. Omit for a blank tab.

profile.description: Chrome profile to open the tab in, by its name or id from browser_list_profiles. Only needed when the user has Tabhand in several profiles. Your later tabs open there too.

tools.name: browser_list_profiles
tools.description: List the Chrome profiles that have Tabhand (for example work and personal, each signed in to different accounts): each one's name, whether Tabhand is on or paused there, and which one your new tabs open in.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Load a URL in one of this session's tabs and wait for it to finish loading.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Read the page as an accessibility outline (headings, text, links, buttons, fields). Elements you can act on carry a ref like e123 for browser_click and browser_type; plain elements the page made clickable show as "clickable". Refs stop working after the page changes, so take a new snapshot then.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element by its ref from browser_snapshot, or else by the text it shows. Waits for any page load the click starts. Links and popups that open a new tab stay in the background, join this session, and are listed in the result. Clicking an option of a dropdown chooses it.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. e123.

text.description: Instead of a ref: the visible text of the element to click, for something the snapshot gives no ref but you can see in a screenshot.

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description: Move the pointer over an element and leave it there, to reveal controls that only show on hover (a delete button on an image, a menu that opens under the pointer). Pass its ref from browser_snapshot, or else the text it shows. Waits a moment for what the hover brings up, then returns a fresh snapshot, so what appeared has refs you can click. If a card or menu is still loading, take another browser_snapshot.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. e123.

text.description: Instead of a ref: the visible text of the element to hover.

tools.name: browser_drag
tools.description: Drag one element onto another: press on the first, move to the second in small steps, and let go. For reordering lists and boards, moving cards between columns, and the like. Works with the browser's own drag and drop and with pages that follow the mouse themselves, and scrolls while holding the item if the drop target is out of sight. Name each end by its ref from browser_snapshot, or else by the text it shows. Says what moved where when the page shows it; take a new snapshot to check the result.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

fromRef.description: Ref of the element to drag, from browser_snapshot, e.g. e123.

fromText.description: Instead of fromRef: the visible text of the element to drag.

toRef.description: Ref of the element to drop it on, from browser_snapshot.

toText.description: Instead of toRef: the visible text of the element to drop it on.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type text into a field. Pass the field's ref to focus it first; omit ref to type into whatever already has focus. Set clear to replace the existing text and submit to press Enter afterwards. Given a dropdown's ref, chooses the option with that text.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

ref.description: Field ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. e123.

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description: Press a key in the page: Enter, Tab, Escape, Backspace, Delete, ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Space, a single character, or a combination such as Shift+Tab.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

key.description: Key or combination, e.g. Enter or Shift+Tab.

tools.name: browser_handle_dialog
tools.description: Answer a confirm or prompt dialog the page opened: accept it (OK) or dismiss it (Cancel). The page waits until it is answered. Alerts are closed for you. Ask the user first if accepting would send, buy, delete or change something.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

accept.description: true for OK, false for Cancel.

text.description: What to enter, for a prompt dialog.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page up or down, e.g. to load more content or bring something into view for a screenshot.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of one of this session's tabs, even though it is in the background. Prefer browser_snapshot for reading text; use screenshots to check layout and visuals.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

fullPage.description: Capture the whole page instead of the visible area (capped at 8000 px tall).

tools.name: browser_list_tabs
tools.description: List the tabs this session has open. Other sessions' tabs and the user's own tabs are never shown.

tools.name: browser_upload_file
tools.description: Attach files from this computer to the page, as if the user picked them. Pass the ref of a file field, or of the button that opens a file picker (no system dialog appears).

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

ref.description: Ref of the file field, or of the button that opens the file picker.

paths.description: Files to attach: absolute paths, or relative to the directory you run in.

tools.name: browser_close_tab
tools.description: Close one of this session's tabs when you are done with it.

tabId.description: Tab id from browser_open_tab or browser_list_tabs.

instructions:
Tabhand gives you the user's own Chrome, signed in to their accounts, in background tabs that never interrupt them.

Use it whenever a task needs a real browser: pages behind a login (email, dashboards, admin panels, social media), web apps without an API, or checking how a site looks and behaves. Prefer it over fetching URLs directly when a page needs the user's session or runs on JavaScript.

How it works:
- browser_open_tab opens a tab in your own tab group; you can only reach tabs you opened and tabs those pages open.
- browser_snapshot reads the page and labels what you can act on with refs like e12; browser_click, browser_type, browser_hover and browser_drag take those refs. Take a new snapshot after the page changes. If something you can see has no ref, browser_click, browser_hover and browser_drag can take its text instead.
- Controls that only appear while the pointer is over something: browser_hover it, and the snapshot it returns shows them. To reorder or move things, browser_drag one onto another.
- Prefer snapshots for reading; use browser_screenshot to check visuals.
- Close your tabs with browser_close_tab when you're done.
- The user may have Tabhand in several Chrome profiles (say, work and personal), each signed in to different accounts. When they mention one, or a tool says Tabhand is paused, call browser_list_profiles, then pass the profile to browser_open_tab. If it's unclear which profile they mean, ask them.

You act as the user, with their accounts: ask before sending messages, posting, buying, deleting or changing settings. If a tool says Chrome isn't connected, ask the user to open Chrome and make sure the Tabhand extension is turned on.
